fun_facts: Blackfin tuna hunt in short violent bursts: they slam into a school of baitfish to scatter it, then wheel back through the scattered fish to pick off stragglers one at a time, rather than simply chasing prey down in a straight line.

Unlike most tuna, which range across entire oceans, blackfin tuna live nowhere but the western Atlantic, and only in water warmer than about 20°C -- one reason they show up off South Carolina in the warm months and disappear the moment the water cools.

It's the smallest member of the true tuna genus Thunnus, topping out around 40 inches and 45 pounds, yet it's also one of the quickest: anglers who hook one report bursts near 40 mph, fast enough to strip line as hard as tuna many times its size.

measures.label: Fork length
measures.help: Measured along the curve of the body, from the tip of the upper jaw to the fork of the tail; curved fork length is the standard tuna measurement.

vocabs.label: Sex
vocabs.help: Blackfin tuna cannot be sexed externally in the field; unknown is the normal answer.

not_taggable.reason: a fish in poor condition or bleeding is unlikely to survive release, so tagging it wastes the tag and the reward
